root_cause.text: In xprtrdma's rpcrdma_post_recvs(), the re_receiving reference counter was incremented but not decremented on early-return paths, leaving the receive-queue drain state permanently active and causing rpcrdma_xprt_drain() to wait forever.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes two early exits from `goto out;` to `goto out_dec;` immediately after `atomic_inc_return(&ep->re_receiving)`, and the commit/CVE text explicitly states that if work request creation fails or exits early, `ep->re_receiving` "will never reach zero and the completion will never be triggered," leading to a hang in `rpcrdma_xprt_drain()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rpcrdma_post_recvs to decrement re_receiving when skipping duplicate receive posting attempts.
intent_record.what: The jump target in rpcrdma_post_recvs() was changed so that when atomic_inc_return(&ep->re_receiving) > 1, control goes to out_dec instead of out.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when another receive-posting operation is already in progress, this path now executes the cleanup/decrement logic associated with out_dec before exiting, preventing the re_receiving counter from being left incorrectly incremented and avoiding inconsistent receive-posting state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the no-work-request path in `rpcrdma_post_recvs()` to use the decrement/rollback exit path and keep receive posting state consistent.
intent_record.what: The conditional branch after building receive work requests was changed so that when `wr` is null, control jumps to `out_dec` instead of `out`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now follows the cleanup/accounting path associated with `out_dec` when no receive work request was prepared, rather than exiting through `out`; this ensures the corresponding decrement or state rollback at `out_dec` occurs and avoids leaving internal counters or bookkeeping inconsistent.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a dedicated exit label so early-exit paths still decrement re_receiving and signal completion correctly.
intent_record.what: A new label named "out_dec:" was inserted immediately before the block that decrements ep->re_receiving with atomic_dec_return() and conditionally calls complete(&ep->re_done); the existing "out:" label remains after that block.
intent_record.how: This creates a distinct jump target so error or early-exit paths can branch directly to the re_receiving decrement/completion logic before continuing to the common exit code, ensuring the receive-posting in-progress counter is properly balanced on those paths.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure all early-exit and no-op paths in rpcrdma_post_recvs() consistently roll back re_receiving and perform completion signaling via a shared exit path.

On the duplicate-posting early-return path and the no-work-request early-return path, that increment was not rolled back, leaking the counter and leaving drain state permanently active.
This early exit is the path that bypassed the later decrement of re_receiving after it had already been incremented, causing the reference count leak described in the root cause.
